eye: pupil of the holotype as described; side not stated for this character (the Methods take mensural and meristic data 'on the right side of the body where possible')
method: qualitative description of the holotype in the formal species description; per Materials and methods the specimens were fixed in 8% formaldehyde and stored in 70% ethanol
conditions: One specimen: holotype ZSI-R-27672, adult male, Kalinga Ghati, Kandhamal District, Odisha State, India (as printed). Type series as printed: holotype ZSI-R-27672 (adult male) and five paratypes, ZSI-R-28076 (adult male, Barbara, Khordha District), ZSI-R-28932 (adult male, Budhakhol, Ganjam District), ZSI-R-29007 (adult female, Barbara, Khordha District), ZSI-R-29247 and 29248 (adult females, Mandaragiri, Angul District). The pupil is described for the holotype only; the word 'pupil' occurs nowhere else in the article (Diagnosis, Colouration, Variations and Comparison print none). Materials and methods (pieces joined): 'The specimens were fixed in 8% formaldehyde solution by injecting the solution into the body and were later stored in 70% ethanol after overnight soaking in the formaldehyde solution.' The 'Description of the holotype' heading says neither 'in life' nor 'in preservation', so whether the pupil was read on the live or preserved animal, and its constriction state, are not stated. Pupil shape is a structural character of the iris and is filed at species level on the same basis as the holotype row for Liuixalus feii on main (recheck-quotes-3); it rests on one specimen.

quote: Eye small (OD/HL ratio 0.3); pupil vertical with serrated margins; supraciliaries small, pointed, those at the anterior end of orbit slightly larger, posterior half with smaller spinose scales.
